claims.text: The repository source only says linked-list odd/even split and does not specify whether parity refers to node position or node value, whether output is two lists or one reordered list, or whether mutation is allowed.

The OpenJDK 21 fixture validates stable two-list splitting for both position parity and value parity, including empty/single/negative-value cases and 2000 deterministic random inputs against independent array-filter oracles.
Both implementations reuse original nodes and explicitly detach old next edges, so they intentionally mutate input topology while avoiding stale cross-links between output lists.
Each node is visited once and appended to exactly one tail with constant pointer work, so both implementations are O(n) time with O(1) auxiliary pointer state excluding the reused output nodes.

findings: The answer does not silently guess the under-specified meaning of odd/even; it exposes both position-parity and value-parity contracts.
